content:
President Donald Trump’s warm greeting for Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday went viral on social media as critics expressed their outright disgust over the encounter.

“Who is he?” Trump asked when he walked into the room and spotted Putin. He chuckled, then answered his own question: “He’s my friend!”

The two shook hands, and Trump said “nice to see you” twice, then leaned over and said something in Putin’s ear.

“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time,” Trump said to the cameras, adding that he thinks “wonderful things” could emerge from the meeting.

Putin has been treated as a pariah by much of the West since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine and the brutal war that has followed, which has led to an estimated 18,000 civilian deaths and left millions displaced. Putin has also orchestrated the forced transfer of thousands of Ukrainian children to Russia ― a move that the United Nations has called both a crime against humanity and a war crime.

But Trump rolled out a literal red carpet for Putin when the two met in Alaska last year, has praised him publicly, and last month struck a deal to import Russian diesel fuel into the United States.

And on Thursday, he called Putin “my friend” and later said it was an “honor” to meet with him.
